description:
Subject:
removal of the remaining side roofslope of the existing back addition at second
floor level to form a roof terrace, enclosed with a 1.8 metre high balustrade; installation of
French doors to the rear elevation of the proposed back addition at second floor level, to
provide access to the proposed roof terrace;

Body:
Following the recent approval of our previous planning application, we are now submitting a standalone application for the inclusion of a roof terrace on the approved flat roof area. To facilitate safe and integrated access to this space, the proposal includes the replacement of the previously approved window with high-quality French doors.

We have carefully reviewed the LBHF Local Plan (2018) and the Planning Guidance SPD. Consequently, this proposal avoids "traditional" open-railing designs. Instead, it offers a highly engineered, policy-compliant solution designed specifically to mitigate the concerns of Policy HO11 and Policy DC4.

Compliance with Local Plan 2018 & Planning Guidance SPD: 
We believe this proposal fully complies with the current regulatory framework through the following measures:

Elimination of Overlooking (Policy HO11): The design incorporates a 0.6m masonry wall and a 1.2m solid privacy panel system, creating a continuous 1.8m physical barrier from the finished floor level. This height exceeds standard eye level, ensuring no direct line of sight into neighboring private amenity spaces or windows.

Acoustic Mitigation and Quiet Use Profile:
Unlike "historic" permeable railings, our proposal uses solid screening to act as a localized acoustic baffle.

It is worth noting that a similar terraces at 28 Epirus Road (Ref: 2019/01497/FUL) and 36 Epirus Road (Ref: 2019/F00862/FFUL) were accepted by the council. Our proposal further mitigates noise by situating the terrace adjacent to a home office/study. This internal room acts as a physical buffer and ensures the intensity of use remains low, quiet, and non-disruptive to neighbors, in line with Key Principle HS7.

Architectural Subservience & Scale (Policy DC4):
Adhering to the council’s preference for subservient additions, the terrace is limited to the rear portion of the roof. The existing roof area is split between the enclosed study and the open terrace for which we are raising this application. The external amenity space occupies less than 50% of the total existing roof length.

Biodiversity and Visual Softening:
To further soften the visual impact, the design incorporates integrated planters. This green screening enhances the host building's character and supports local biodiversity while providing a natural visual and sound buffer for the streetscape.

Access and External Alterations:
The transition from the approved window to French doors has been designed to match the architectural language and materials of the existing dwelling, ensuring a high-quality finish that respects the host building.
